task.title: Enabling image pull activity tracking
task.shortdesc: To enable image pull activity tracking in Red Hat Quay, you can set FEATURE_IMAGE_PULL_STATS in your config.yaml file and configure Redis for pull metrics.

step.cmd: In your Red Hat Quay config.yaml file, set FEATURE_IMAGE_PULL_STATS: true. For example:

info.codeblock: # ... FEATURE_IMAGE_PULL_STATS: true REDIS_FLUSH_INTERVAL_SECONDS: 30 PULL_METRICS_REDIS: host: <redis_host> password: <redis_password> port: 6379 db: 1 # ...

dlentry.dd: Specifies whether image pull tracking activity is enabled.

Specifies the time, in seconds, at which the Redis flush worker clears old data. Shorter intervals keep data fresher and help prevent Redis from bloating, while longer intervals reduce flush frequency.
Specifies the connection settings for the Redis database used to store image pull metrics.

step.cmd: Restart your Red Hat Quay deployment.

ol.li: Push an image to your registry by entering the following command. Following this step, you can use your browser to see the tagged image in your repository. $ podman push <quay-server.example.com>/<organization>/<image>:<tag>
Pull the image from your Red Hat Quay registry by entering the following command: $ podman pull <quay-server.example.com>/<organization>/<image>:<tag>
On the Red Hat Quay UI, navigate to Repositories, and then click the name of your repository.

Click Tags. The Last Pulled and Pull Count categories show you information about when the image was last pulled, and how many times it has been pulled, respectively. For example:
